Michael Jordan’s 10 scoring titles and LeBron James’s all-time career scoring record represent two fundamentally different philosophies in basketball debates: **peak scoring dominance** versus **career longevity and cumulative volume**.

---

### 1. The Argument for Peak Dominance: Michael Jordan’s Scoring Titles
Jordan’s scoring titles anchor the argument that at his peak, no player dominated individual scoring races more completely or maintained higher game-to-game scoring output:

* **Unrivaled Peak Dominance:** Jordan won 10 NBA scoring titles [T1, jordan_scoring_0]. He captured his first in his third season, won seven consecutively, and claimed his tenth in his final Bulls season (1997–98) [jordan_scoring_80].
* **Per-Game Scoring Supremacy:** Over 15 seasons and 1,072 career regular-season games, Jordan averaged 30.1 points per game, compared to LeBron’s 26.8 points per game [T3, T4, T5]. 
* **High-Ceiling Explosiveness:** Jordan logged 173 regular-season games with 40+ points and 31 games with 50+ points (compared to LeBron's 79 and 14, respectively) [T3, T4].
* **Volume and Efficiency:** In NBA history, seasons with over 30 points per 75 possessions at +6% relative true shooting (rTS) occurred only 11 times, and Jordan owns four of them [jordan_defense_2720]. 
* **Tradeoff / Counterpoint:** Evidence notes that Jordan's scoring focus could lead him to lock stubbornly into scoring mode, sometimes probing for his own shot rather than making high-percentage passes [jordan_defense_640].

---

### 2. The Argument for Sustained Excellence and Longevity: LeBron James’s Career Scoring Record
LeBron’s career scoring mark underpins the argument that durability, sustained consistency across decades, and all-time cumulative production represent the pinnacle of offensive greatness:

* **All-Time Cumulative Benchmark:** LeBron broke Kareem Abdul-Jabbar’s scoring record to become the NBA's all-time scoring leader [lebron_scoring_240, lebron_scoring_320, lebron_longevity_560].
* **Multi-Decade Consistency:** LeBron sustained scoring averages of at least 25 points per game in all 19 seasons following his 2003–04 rookie year [lebron_scoring_240], playing across 23 seasons and 1,622 career games [T4].
* **Consistent High-Floor Output:** Although LeBron has won 1 scoring title [T2], his sustained availability and consistency enabled him to amass 577 games with 30+ points, surpassing Jordan's total of 562 [T3, T4].
* **Tradeoff / Counterpoint:** While LeBron amassed the all-time scoring record through prolonged durability, his per-game regular-season scoring rate (26.8 PPG) and single-season scoring titles (1) are lower than Jordan's (30.1 PPG and 10 titles) [T1, T2, T5].

---

### Factual Evidence vs. Subjective GOAT Judgments

* **Factual Evidence:** Jordan holds the clear edge in regular-season scoring average (30.1 to 26.8 PPG) [T5], scoring titles (10 to 1) [T1, T2], and 40+/50+ point games [T3, T4]. LeBron holds the clear edge in career games played (1,622 to 1,072) [T3, T4], 30+ point games (577 to 562) [T3, T4], and total career scoring, having surpassed Kareem Abdul-Jabbar as the NBA's all-time leading scorer [lebron_scoring_240].
* **Subjective GOAT Judgment:** Deciding which record is superior depends entirely on subjective criteria: whether one values an era-defining, unbeatable per-game peak (Jordan's 10 scoring titles) over unprecedented, multi-decade durability and total offensive accumulation (LeBron's all-time scoring crown).
